title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
What makes data tidy?

Each variable is a column
Each observation is a row
Each value is a cell


Tidy data is the shape dplyr and ggplot2 expect. Most of your time cleaning data goes into getting it there.

section: Our data: COVID-19 testing at CHOP
text:
Our data: COVID-19 testing at CHOP
15,524 tests from the first 107 days of the pandemic at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (medicaldata::covid_testing). One row = one test, not one person.

glimpse(covid)

Rows: 15,524
Columns: 17
$ subject_id      <int> 1412, 533, 9134, 8518, 8967, 11048, 663, 215…
$ fake_first_name <chr> "jhezane", "penny", "grunt", "melisandre", "…
$ fake_last_name  <chr> "westerling", "targaryen", "rivers", "swyft"…
$ gender          <chr> "female", "female", "male", "female", "male"…
$ pan_day         <int> 4, 7, 7, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9,…
$ test_id         <chr> "covid", "covid", "covid", "covid", "covid",…
$ clinic_name     <chr> "inpatient ward a", "clinical lab", "clinica…
$ result          <chr> "negative", "negative", "negative", "negativ…
$ demo_group      <chr> "patient", "patient", "patient", "patient", …
$ age             <dbl> 0.0, 0.0, 0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 0.0, 0.0,…
$ drive_thru_ind  <int> 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1,…
$ ct_result       <dbl> 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, 45, …
$ orderset        <int> 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1,…
$ payor_group     <chr> "government", "commercial", NA, NA, "governm…
$ patient_class   <chr> "inpatient", "not applicable", NA, NA, "emer…
$ col_rec_tat     <dbl> 1.4, 2.3, 7.3, 5.8, 1.2, 1.4, 2.6, 0.7, 1.0,…
$ rec_ver_tat     <dbl> 5.2, 5.8, 4.7, 5.0, 6.4, 7.0, 4.2, 6.3, 5.6,…

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Read |> as “and then”

covid |>
  filter(result == "positive") |>
  count(clinic_name)



Take covid, and then keep the positive tests, and then count them by clinic.



Without the pipe, the same code reads inside-out:

count(filter(covid, result == "positive"), clinic_name)




Shortcut: Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + M types |>. You may also see %>%. It works the same way for our purposes.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
filter(): keep rows that match

covid |>
  filter(result == "positive")

# A tibble: 865 × 17
  subject_id fake_first_name fake_last_name gender pan_day test_id
       <int> <chr>           <chr>          <chr>    <int> <chr>  
1       2114 azzak           tully          male        10 covid  
2       7240 arryk           mormont        male        11 covid  
3      11391 zei             umber          female      11 covid  
4        902 owen            seaworth       male        12 covid  
5       2573 glendon         lannister      male        12 covid  
# ℹ 860 more rows
# ℹ 11 more variables: clinic_name <chr>, result <chr>,
#   demo_group <chr>, age <dbl>, drive_thru_ind <int>,
#   ct_result <dbl>, orderset <int>, payor_group <chr>,
#   patient_class <chr>, col_rec_tat <dbl>, rec_ver_tat <dbl>

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Multiple conditions

# both must be true: comma (or &)
covid |> filter(result == "positive", age >= 18)

# either can be true: |
covid |> filter(clinic_name == "nicu" | clinic_name == "picu")

# match any value in a list: %in%
covid |> filter(clinic_name %in% c("nicu", "picu"))

# not equal
covid |> filter(result != "invalid")








Warning


= assigns, == compares. filter(result = "positive") is an error.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Your turn: filter()
Keep the tests collected at the emergency dept that were positive. How many rows?

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
arrange(): sort rows

covid |>
  select(subject_id, age, demo_group) |>
  arrange(desc(age))

# A tibble: 15,524 × 3
  subject_id   age demo_group 
       <int> <dbl> <chr>      
1       3049   138 client     
2       4078   119 patient    
3      12293   119 other adult
4      11177   119 client     
5        337   119 misc adult 
# ℹ 15,519 more rows



An age of 138? Sorting is a fast way to catch data errors.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
select(): keep columns

covid |>
  select(subject_id, age, result)

# A tibble: 15,524 × 3
  subject_id   age result  
       <int> <dbl> <chr>   
1       1412   0   negative
2        533   0   negative
3       9134   0.8 negative
4       8518   0.8 negative
5       8967   0.8 negative
# ℹ 15,519 more rows

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
select() helpers

covid |> select(subject_id:gender)      # a range
covid |> select(-fake_first_name, -fake_last_name)  # drop
covid |> select(starts_with("demo"))   # by name pattern
covid |> select(ends_with("_tat"))
covid |> select(where(is.numeric))     # by type

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
mutate(): add or change columns

covid |>
  mutate(
    age_months = age * 12,
    positive   = result == "positive"
  ) |>
  select(subject_id, age, age_months, result, positive)

# A tibble: 15,524 × 5
  subject_id   age age_months result   positive
       <int> <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>    <lgl>   
1       1412   0          0   negative FALSE   
2        533   0          0   negative FALSE   
3       9134   0.8        9.6 negative FALSE   
4       8518   0.8        9.6 negative FALSE   
5       8967   0.8        9.6 negative FALSE   
# ℹ 15,519 more rows




mutate() returns a new data frame. Save it with <- if you want to keep the change.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
count()

covid |>
  count(result)

# A tibble: 3 × 2
  result       n
  <chr>    <int>
1 invalid    301
2 negative 14358
3 positive   865




covid |>
  count(clinic_name, sort = TRUE)

# A tibble: 88 × 2
  clinic_name           n
  <chr>             <int>
1 clinical lab       7500
2 emergency dept     3413
3 oncology day hosp   533
4 nicu                294
5 laboratory          270
# ℹ 83 more rows

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
summarize(): collapse to one row

covid |>
  summarize(
    n_tests      = n(),
    mean_age     = mean(age),
    pct_positive = mean(result == "positive") * 100
  )

# A tibble: 1 × 3
  n_tests mean_age pct_positive
    <int>    <dbl>        <dbl>
1   15524     14.2         5.57



Why does mean(result == "positive") give a proportion? TRUE counts as 1 and FALSE as 0.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Missing values

covid |>
  summarize(mean_ct = mean(ct_result))

# A tibble: 1 × 1
  mean_ct
    <dbl>
1      NA




covid |>
  summarize(mean_ct = mean(ct_result, na.rm = TRUE))

# A tibble: 1 × 1
  mean_ct
    <dbl>
1    44.1





One NA makes the whole mean NA. Use na.rm = TRUE, and think about why values are missing.

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Your turn: grouped summary
For each demo_group, find the number of tests and the median age.

text:

title: Data wrangling I: tidy data & dplyr
text:
Recap



Verb
Works on
Does




filter()
rows
keeps rows that meet a condition


arrange()
rows
sorts rows


select()
columns
keeps or drops columns


mutate()
columns
adds or changes columns


summarize()
groups
collapses to one row per group


count()
groups
shortcut for counting

title: HW 04: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Data
covid_testing from the medicaldata package: 15,524 COVID-19 tests from the first 107 days of the pandemic at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia. It’s the same data as the lab. Run ?covid_testing in the Console for the codebook.

title: HW 04: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Questions
Write your code in the chunks provided. Answer the written parts in complete sentences below each chunk, outside the code.
1. Getting oriented (2 pts). Load the packages and use glimpse() on covid_testing. How many rows and columns are there? What does one row represent?
2. Tests vs. people (2 pts). Use n_distinct() to count the number of unique people (subject_id). Why is this number smaller than the number of rows?
3. Filtering (3 pts).

How many tests had an "invalid" result?
How many tests were collected in the NICU or PICU (clinic_name is "nicu" or "picu")? Use %in%.

4. A data quality check (3 pts). Use arrange() to look at the oldest ages in the data.

How many tests have an age over 100?
Create a new data frame covid_clean that removes those rows. Use covid_clean for the rest of the assignment.
In one or two sentences, explain why you think those values are in the data, and whether removing them is the right call.

5. Creating variables (3 pts). Using covid_clean, add two columns with mutate():

age_group: "child" if age is under 18, otherwise "adult" (use if_else())
positive: TRUE if the result is "positive", otherwise FALSE

Save the result back to covid_clean, then use count() to show how many tests are in each age_group.
6. Grouped summaries (4 pts). Excluding invalid tests, compute the number of tests and the percent positive:

for each age_group
for each demo_group, sorted from highest to lowest percent positive
Write two sentences describing what you found.

7. Early vs. later in the pandemic (2 pts). pan_day is the day of the pandemic the sample was collected. Create a variable period that is "early" for days 1–50 and "later" for days 51 and up. Compare the percent positive between the two periods (excluding invalid tests).
8. Reflection (1 pt). Name one question about COVID-19 in Philadelphia that this data cannot answer, and explain why. (Hint: who gets tested at a children’s hospital?)

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
The data
covid holds 15,524 COVID-19 tests from the first 107 days of the pandemic at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia (from the medicaldata package). Names in the data are fake. Some of the columns:







Column
Meaning




subject_id
Person tested


gender
Gender


age
Age in years


pan_day
Day of the pandemic the test was collected (day 1 = start of data)


clinic_name
Where the sample was collected


result
"positive", "negative", or "invalid"


demo_group
"patient", "client", "misc adult", "other adult", "unidentified"


drive_thru_ind
1 = collected at a drive-through site, 0 = not


ct_result
PCR cycle threshold (45 = virus not detected)



Run this block to take a look:

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Part 1: Is it tidy?
Remember the three rules of tidy data: each variable is a column, each observation is a row, and each value is a cell.






TipQuestion: What is one row of covid? Think, then click to check.





One row is one test. Some people were tested more than once, so one row is not one person. That matters when you count: nrow(covid) counts tests, not people.









TipQuestion: Imagine a table with one row per clinic and a separate column for each pandemic day’s test count. Is that tidy?





No. “Day” is a variable, but in that table its values are spread across column names. You’ll learn to fix that shape with pivot_longer() next week.

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Part 2: Working with rows

Exercise 1: filter()
Keep only the positive tests.









result is a character column, so the value goes in quotes: "positive".


covid |>
  filter(result == "positive")
There are 865 positive tests.






Exercise 2: filter() with two conditions
Keep positive tests from people who are 18 or older.









Separating conditions with a comma inside filter() means both must be true. Use >= for “greater than or equal to.”


covid |>
  filter(result == "positive", age >= 18)






Exercise 3: arrange()
Sort the tests from oldest to youngest person. Look at the top of the result.









arrange() sorts smallest-to-largest by default. Wrap the column in desc() to reverse it.


covid |>
  select(subject_id, age, demo_group) |>
  arrange(desc(age))










ImportantThink about it: what’s wrong with the top rows?





The oldest “person” is 138, and several are 119. Those ages are almost certainly data entry errors or placeholder values. Real data always needs a sanity check before analysis. Sorting is one of the quickest ways to find problems.

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Part 3: Working with columns

Exercise 4: select()
Keep only the columns subject_id, age, clinic_name, and result, in that order.









List the column names inside select(), separated by commas. No quotes needed.


covid |>
  select(subject_id, age, clinic_name, result)






Exercise 5: mutate()
Add a new column age_months that is age in months.









There are 12 months in a year. Columns can be used in arithmetic: age * 2.


covid |>
  mutate(age_months = age * 12) |>
  select(subject_id, age, age_months)

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Part 4: Summarizing

Exercise 6: count()
How many tests came from each clinic_name? Show the largest first.









count() has an argument sort. Set it to TRUE.


covid |>
  count(clinic_name, sort = TRUE)






Exercise 7: group_by() + summarize()
Were drive-through tests more likely to be positive? For each value of drive_thru_ind, compute the number of tests (n) and the percent positive (pct_positive).









Group by the column that marks drive-through tests.
Why does mean(result == "positive") work? result == "positive" gives TRUE/FALSE, which R treats as 1/0. The mean of 1s and 0s is a proportion.


covid |>
  group_by(drive_thru_ind) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    pct_positive = mean(result == "positive") * 100
  )






Exercise 8: your turn, from scratch
Find the median age for each demo_group. Call the summary column median_age.









Same pattern as Exercise 7: group_by() then summarize(). Use median(age).


covid |>
  group_by(demo_group) |>
  summarize(median_age = median(age))

title: Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
Lab 05: Data wrangling with dplyr
text:
Wrap-up
You used the five core dplyr verbs today:



Verb
Does what to the data




filter()
keeps rows that meet a condition


arrange()
sorts rows


select()
keeps columns


mutate()
adds or changes columns


group_by() + summarize()
collapses each group to one row



Next: HW 04 practices these verbs in RStudio. The Week 5 cheat sheet has all the syntax on one page.
